corrected_value.title: Eco-Friendliness in the Brand Experience of High-Tech Products.

decision.location: Research Method and Data, line 49; Conclusions, line 97; Reference 19, line 273
decision.quote: In this study we replicate the extended BXS [19] cross-nationally to measure differences in the ways consumers experience the eco-friendliness of global smartphone brands in a cross-national context. The survey items were selected from the previously developed and extended BXS [18,19,107]. We assess the four items measuring eco-friendliness as well as the other four brand experience dimensions from the BXS by conducting structural equation modeling (SEM) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) following the same steps that Brakus et al. [18] undertook.
decision.reason: The paper collects cross-national survey data in Finland (N = 506) and India (N = 502) and empirically re-tests via CFA and SEM both the original 4-dimension Brand Experience Scale (BXS) of Brakus et al. (2009) [18] and the 4-item eco-friendliness BXS extension developed and initially confirmed in one Western country by Saari (2016) [19] ('Saari, U. Eco-Friendliness in the Brand Experience of High-Tech Products. Ph.D. Thesis, Tampere University of Technology, Tampere, Finland, 2016.', no DOI printed), evaluating factor loadings (>0.50), AVE (0.62 in India, 0.70 in Finland), CR (0.86 in India, 0.90 in Finland), and Cronbach's alpha (0.851 and 0.899) for the eco-friendliness dimension across both countries. The only shipped row (input_row_index 592, 10.1509/jmkg.73.3.052) is Brakus, Schmitt, and Zarantonello (2009) [18], a distinct 2009 journal article by different authors that established the original 4-dimension BXS without an eco-friendliness dimension, so report equivalence does not apply. The prior adjudication also concluded blind_right for this missing target (failing validation only due to legacy schema keys).

In the Introduction, the authors explicitly state that they examined the reproducibility of the intestinal dysbiosis findings in murine models of HSCR and HAEC reported by both Ward et al.
